system.name: Radical
system.one_liner: a system that lets strongly consistent applications run near users by performing all coordination in a single linearizable LVI request overlapped with speculative execution

components.name: Near-User Location
components.role: an edge site (repeated twice, symmetric) running application logic close to users

components.name: Radical
components.role: the near-user runtime library and function-execution environment

components.name: Function Execution
components.role: executes the application function speculatively alongside the read/write-set-finding function

components.name: f_rw
components.role: function executed first to find the request's read/write set, sent as part of the LVI request

components.name: f
components.role: the application function speculatively executed while the LVI request is in flight

components.name: Storage Library
components.role: Radical's library through which the speculatively executing function f communicates with the local cache

components.name: Radical Runtime
components.role: coordinates local execution and the LVI Request/Followup exchange with the near-storage location

components.name: Cache
components.role: local key/value/version cache backing speculative execution

components.name: Near-Storage Location
components.role: the central site hosting the shared LVI Server and Primary Storage

components.name: LVI Server
components.role: server handling LVI Requests and Followups from all near-user locations

components.name: LVI Handler
components.role: handles incoming LVI Requests against Primary Storage

components.name: Followup Handler
components.role: handles Followup messages, resolving write intents, invoking Backup Functions on timeout

components.name: Primary Storage
components.role: durable storage at the near-storage location holding write intents, data, and backup functions

components.name: Write Intents
components.role: table (Execution ID, Status) tracking in-flight LVI requests

components.name: Data
components.role: table (Key, Value, Version) of stored data

components.name: Backup Functions
components.role: fallback functions the Followup Handler can invoke, apparently on a timeout, to resolve an unfinished write intent

flows.what: LVI Request carrying the read/write set found by f_rw
speculative execution of f communicates with the cache
invokes a backup function, apparently on timeout, to complete an unresolved write intent

content.key_idea: Each near-user Radical runtime speculatively executes a function against a local cache while sending only the precomputed read/write set to a single near-storage LVI server, which linearizes the request with locks, validation, and write intents, hiding the near-storage round trip behind the speculative execution.
content.reading_order: Left to right: a Near-User Location's Radical runtime executes f_rw and speculatively runs f against its Cache via the Storage Library, sending an LVI Request/Followup to the central Near-Storage Location's LVI Server, mirrored by a second Near-User Location on the right.

style.stroke: thin (~0.73pt) uniform black outlines, no dashing
style.font: serif (Linux Libertine / LibertineMath), about 4.5-8.5pt, italic for function symbols (f, f_rw)
style.arrows: thin black single- and double-headed arrows, orthogonal and diagonal, no special styling
style.icons: vector, small person/user silhouette icons flanking each Near-User Location, and a small clock/stopwatch icon near the Followup-Handler-to-Backup-Functions arrow suggesting a timeout trigger

encoding.emphasis: the strict left-right mirror symmetry between the two Near-User Location panels, both funneling into the single central Near-Storage Location, visually argues that the LVI protocol scales to many symmetric near-user sites coordinating through one shared near-storage server
reusable_patterns: central server location flanked symmetrically by repeated identical peer-location panels
a small clock icon on an arrow to denote a timeout-triggered fallback path
weaknesses: with no color or line-style coding at all, the many similarly-drawn double-headed arrows between handlers and storage tables are hard to tell apart without carefully tracing each one

evidence: Radical's runtime begins by executing frw to find the read/write set
speculatively executing the f, which communicates with the cache through Radical's storage library
Radical's architecture is illustrated in Figure 2, which depicts near-user and near storage locations

summary: Radical lets strongly consistent applications run close to users (in nearby datacenters, edge points of presence, or on-premises) by performing all necessary coordination in one linearizable LVI request, hiding its latency behind speculative execution. Figure 2 draws this as a hub-and-spoke architecture: a central 'Near-Storage Location' hosting an LVI Server (with an LVI Handler and Followup Handler over a Primary Storage of Write Intents, Data, and Backup Functions) is flanked symmetrically by two 'Near-User Location' instances, each running Radical (Function Execution of f_rw and f, a Storage Library, and a Radical Runtime) over a local Cache. Per the caption, the runtime first executes f_rw to compute the read/write set, sends it to the LVI Server as part of the LVI request, and speculatively executes f against the cache via the storage library; a clock icon marks a timeout-triggered backup-function path at the LVI Server.
